Fully free placement on a square grid. G.DETAIL: The base is a square tile grid. Each tile is one unit. Buildings occupy 1x1 to 4x4 tile footprints depending on size. Walls occupy 1x1 tiles. No terrain features - clean grid like Clash of Clans.
CC1 starts with a 20x20 grid (400 tiles). Each CC level expands the grid by 2-4 tiles per side up to a maximum of 40x40 (1600 tiles) at CC10.
All buildings can be placed on any open tile. No zone restrictions. Players decide their own layout strategy - cluster defenses, spread resources, create kill corridors, or mix freely.
Small buildings (mines, towers): 1x1 or 2x2. Medium buildings (barracks, vaults): 2x2 or 3x3. Large buildings (CC, Dark Barracks, THAAD): 3x3 or 4x4. Footprint listed per building.
A fixed outer wall ring automatically forms along the edge of the current grid boundary. This perimeter is always present and upgrades with the wall tier. Players cannot remove it.
Additional wall tiles are placed freely inside the grid to create internal compartments, funnels, and kill corridors. Players start with 50 tiles at CC1 scaling to 200 at CC10.

A 3-tile wide strip just inside the perimeter is the Dead Zone. Mines and wall tiles can go here but no buildings. This prevents buildings from being placed on the outer edge where they cannot be defended.
Deployment zones sit 5 tiles outside the base grid on all 4 sides. This is open ground where attacking units form up before advancing. No buildings or walls allowed in this buffer.
Players can copy and save up to 3 full base layouts. Useful for switching between a farming layout (resources exposed) and a trophy layout (CC protected). Switching takes 5 seconds.
All buildings and walls can be rotated 90 degrees. Primarily cosmetic but affects which direction tower animations face. Useful for visual clarity in planning.

_notes.Compartmentalization: Divide the base into separate walled sections. When attackers breach one compartment they face another wall before reaching the next. Each breach costs time and exposes units to defenses. Aim for at least 3 compartments at CC5 and 5 compartments at CC10.
_notes.Funnel Points: Create deliberate gaps or weak points in walls that channel attackers into kill zones. Place Bomb Towers and Mortar Towers covering these funnel points. Attackers path toward the gap and cluster perfectly for splash damage.
_notes.Defense Coverage: Every defense tower should cover at least 2 compartments. Towers placed deep inside a compartment only cover that compartment. Towers near compartment edges can fire into adjacent areas through wall gaps.
_notes.Resource Positioning: Early game: place resources in outer compartments as a sacrifice layer. Mid game: move resources to inner compartments once you have enough defenses to punish attackers who go deep. Late game: protect all storage in innermost ring.
_notes.Dragon Teeth Usage: Dragon Teeth cannot be destroyed. Place them at the North perimeter to force Heavy Tanks to path around them. This delays wall breaching and channels attackers into specific entry points covered by Bomb Towers.
_notes.Wall Tile Budget: Do not spend all wall tiles on the outer perimeter. The perimeter wall already exists automatically. Use placeable tiles for internal compartments. A common mistake is walling the perimeter twice wasting tiles.
_notes.Minefield Placement: Place Minefields 2-3 tiles inside the perimeter not on the perimeter itself. Attackers breach the outer wall then hit the Minefield as they flood in. Catching units post-breach maximizes kill count.
_notes.Anti-SPG Design: SPGs fire from the rear without entering the base. Counter by placing high-HP buildings like CC and Dark Barracks away from the South perimeter where SPG rear attacks originate. Sniper Towers can target SPGs before they establish position.
_notes.CIWS Placement: CIWS Towers have very short range. Place them directly next to your highest value buildings - CC, Gold Vault, Dark Barracks. They are a last-resort intercept system not a perimeter defense.
_notes.War Bunker Location: War Bunker garrison deploys when base hits 50% destruction. Place the Bunker centrally so donated troops can reach any part of the base. A Bunker in a corner means garrison units have to cross the entire base under fire.
